answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring a bonded, auditable history before granting influence. Each identity completes random tasks and receives attestations from reviewers outside its social cluster; failed audits raise its bond. A cedar ledger anchors signed work, an atlas maps repeated behavior across tasks, and a meadow queue limits reward claims per identity. Correlated fakes are quarantined and slashed, making mass fabrication progressively more expensive.
